stories.headline: Moody's Combines Proprietary Datasets and Agentic AI to Accelerate Client Credit Decisions
stories.summary: Moody's has rolled out a new capability combining its proprietary datasets, domain expertise, and agentic AI to help clients make faster, more contextualised credit risk decisions — a direct move into the AI Decision Intelligence space D&B is targeting. This is a meaningful competitor signal: Moody's is not just a data licensor but is now positioning its own agentic layer on top of its risk data, competing with D&B's compliance and risk agent proposition. D&B's differentiator here must be entity resolution breadth and DUNS-anchored ground truth that Moody's cannot replicate at the SME and private company level.

stories.headline: HubSpot Closes Warmly Acquisition as GTM Consolidation Wave Reshapes B2B Data Landscape
stories.summary: A verified 2026 acquisition changelog confirms HubSpot acquired Warmly, Zoom acquired Common Room, and Salesforce completed its purchase of Qualified (closed April 1, 2026) — all in the same consolidation cycle that saw Apollo absorb Pocus. The pattern is clear: platforms owning the system of record or system of engagement are hoovering up signal intelligence and buyer intent layers, collapsing the distance between data and action. For D&B, this accelerating consolidation reinforces the urgency of the 'be everywhere' embedding strategy — as standalone GTM data layers get acquired, neutral infrastructure providers become more strategically valuable, not less.

stories.headline: Federal Reserve Publishes New Research on Bank Funding Behind Private Credit — Data Opacity Remains the Core Problem
stories.summary: A Federal Reserve FEDS Note published August 7, 2026 documents how banks charge Business Development Companies a funding premium during monetary tightening, even when loans are senior and collateralised — findings drawn from supervisory loan data most commercial risk platforms cannot access. The research highlights the structural opacity of the private credit market, where bank-assessed internal credit ratings and BDC exposure data sit behind regulatory walls rather than in commercial data products. This is a direct validation of the market gap D&B and peers face: demand for commercial credit intelligence on private, unrated entities is growing faster than the available data supply.

stories.headline: AI Investment Cycle Creates New Underwriting Blind Spots as Hyperscaler Debt Floods Credit Markets
stories.summary: BlackRock's Credit Currents report (August 12, 2026) flags that AI-related financing has become an increasingly dominant driver of credit market supply, with accelerating hyperscaler bond issuance and data centre financing expanding across investment grade and high yield — and pushing pricing wider. Heavy supply and construction risk are making differentiated underwriting more critical, precisely at the moment when standard credit models are least equipped to assess AI infrastructure exposure. For D&B's financial risk and commercial data proposition, this creates a clear use case: firmographic and corporate family tree data that helps underwriters distinguish true AI-infrastructure obligors from adjacent names caught in valuation distortion.

stories.headline: 45% of Enterprise AI Projects Failing to Deliver — CIOs Demanding Governance as Precondition, Not Afterthought
stories.summary: An IDC report from early August 2026 finds that 45% of enterprise AI projects are failing to produce results, with CIOs increasingly demanding clearer ROI, stronger security, and defined governance frameworks for agentic AI deployments. The finding cuts directly against the 'move fast, embed agents everywhere' narrative and elevates the D&B Explainability First positioning: agents built on verifiable, governed ground-truth data have a structural advantage over those running on unvalidated LLM outputs. Organisations that treated governance as a precondition — not an afterthought — are the ones seeing results, which is precisely the argument for anchoring agentic workflows to D&B's DUNS-resolved entity layer.

stories.headline: ElevenLabs Closes Series D with BlackRock and NVIDIA, Crosses $500M ARR
stories.summary: ElevenLabs has surpassed $500 million in annual recurring revenue — up from $350M at end of 2025 — and closed a new tranche of its Series D with institutional heavyweights including BlackRock, Wellington Management, D.E. Shaw, and Schroders joining NVIDIA as backers. The round values the AI voice infrastructure company at $11 billion and underscores that enterprise voice agents for sales, support, and marketing are now a mainstream budget line. For D&B, ElevenLabs is a potential embedded-channel partner: voice agents operating at this scale need entity resolution and buyer-signal data to make contextually intelligent outbound calls.

stories.headline: Alibaba Ships Qwen3.8-27B to Open API — Frontier Open-Weight Race Intensifies
stories.summary: Alibaba's Qwen team released Qwen3.8-27B on August 14, 2026, making it generally available via API at published per-token pricing, with open weights promised but not yet published. It is the most recent entry in a tracked series of 11 frontier model launches since late April, and continues China's pattern of delivering near-frontier performance on openly accessible models. The open-weight trajectory matters strategically: as capable models commoditise, D&B's proprietary data assets — Paydex, DUNS, Buydex, corporate family trees — become the irreplaceable differentiator that any agent running on any model still needs.

stories.headline: EU Delays High-Risk AI Act Deadlines to 2027–2028 After Last-Minute Legislative Fix
stories.summary: The EU Council gave final approval in late June 2026 to postpone the AI Act's high-risk system obligations — which had been due to bite on August 2 — to December 2027 for standalone systems and August 2028 for AI embedded in products. The delay reflects lobbying pressure from industry unprepared for compliance, though transparency obligations (Article 50) and GPAI model rules went live on schedule on August 2. The reprieve gives enterprise AI vendors more runway but also signals that the EU's enforcement posture is more politically negotiable than its rhetoric suggested — a dynamic worth watching as US federal legislation like the FRONTIER Act takes shape.

stories.headline: Neocloud Axe Compute Reports Revenue Up 90x, Crosses $3B in Signed Customer Contracts
stories.summary: Axe Compute, a purpose-built AI infrastructure provider, reported Q2 2026 results showing revenue growth exceeding 90x year-over-year and more than $3 billion in total signed customer contracts — projecting over $696 million in annualised recurring revenue at full deployment. Days later the company announced a 55-megawatt U.S. data centre capacity expansion with Duos Technologies. The numbers validate that demand for dedicated, large-scale AI compute is not consolidating solely with CoreWeave — a growing tier of specialised neoclouds is capturing enterprise workloads, keeping infrastructure economics competitive and reinforcing the case that AI agent compute costs will continue to fall.

stories.headline: Premiership Rugby Scraps Promotion and Relegation — Franchise Model Begins 2026-27
stories.summary: The RFU council voted in February to abolish automatic promotion and relegation between the Premiership and Championship from the 2026-27 season, replacing it with a criteria-based expansion and demotion model. The upcoming season — which starts 25 September 2026 — will therefore be the first ever played under a full franchise structure. It is a seismic structural shift for English club rugby, mirroring moves seen in other major sports leagues.

stories.headline: Trump and Vance Give Contradictory Accounts of Why the US Is at War with Iran
stories.summary: Senior White House figures publicly offered differing explanations for the US military's ongoing conflict with Iran, fuelling confusion over the administration's strategic rationale. The discrepancy, reported on 18 August, highlights fractures in messaging at the highest level as the conflict continues. It follows weeks of escalating US-Iran tensions after diplomatic overtures collapsed.

stories.headline: IAEA Unearths Tons of Nuclear Material at Clandestine Syrian Site — New Regime Refuses Hand-Over
stories.summary: A UN inspection team excavated a previously undisclosed site in Syria and found several tonnes of nuclear material dating from the Assad era. The agreed plan was for the IAEA to remove the material, but Syria's new al-Sharaa-led government has reversed course and is refusing to hand it over. The development raises acute non-proliferation concerns given the regime's links to former al-Qaeda networks.

stories.headline: Hubble Captures Definitive Evidence of Dwarf Galaxy Actively Merging with the Young Milky Way
stories.summary: New data from NASA's Hubble Space Telescope show definitive evidence of a dwarf galaxy in the process of merging with the early Milky Way, shedding fresh light on how our galaxy grew to its current size by consuming smaller neighbours. The findings, published on 17 August, add crucial observational detail to models of galactic formation and evolution. Researchers say the data resolves longstanding questions about the timeline of the Milky Way's early growth phase.

stories.headline: Arsenal Sign Bruno Guimarães for £75m as Premier League Window Heats Up Before Saturday Kick-Off
stories.summary: Arsenal have moved to strengthen their squad ahead of the 2026-27 Premier League season — which kicks off on 22 August — by completing the signing of Newcastle midfielder Bruno Guimarães for £75 million. The summer transfer window, open until 1 September, has also seen Piero Hincapié arrive from Bayer Leverkusen for £34.5m and Christos Tzolis join from Club Brugge for £34m. The business underlines Arsenal's intent to defend the title they won last season under Mikel Arteta.

stories.headline: BMW Championship Lines Up at Bellerive — PGA Tour FedEx Playoffs Reach Penultimate Stage
stories.summary: With the FedEx St. Jude Championship now concluded, the PGA Tour's FedEx Cup playoffs move to their penultimate event, the BMW Championship, scheduled for 27–30 August at Bellerive. The top 50 players in FedExCup points have qualified for the St. Louis event, setting up a high-stakes weekend before the Tour Championship at East Lake. The field includes the leading contenders on the FedExCup standings as the race for the season-ending prize intensifies.

stories.headline: Habitable Worlds Observatory: Inside NASA's $11 Billion Bet to Photograph Another Living Earth
stories.summary: A detailed new report examines the engineering challenges facing NASA's Habitable Worlds Observatory, the next-generation space telescope being designed specifically to directly image Earth-like exoplanets. Key hurdles include building a coronagraph that must block ten billion times a planet's light and a picometer-stable mirror that does not yet exist. Scientists say successfully reading an exoplanet's atmosphere for biosignatures — oxygen, methane, ozone, water — will still be extraordinarily difficult even with the new instrument.

stories.headline: Stripe Acquiring OpenRouter, Aggregating AI?, Flipping the Business Model
stories.summary: Ben Thompson's August 17 Stratechery analysis frames Stripe's $7B+ acquisition of OpenRouter not as a payments deal but as a bet on AI Aggregation Theory — the idea that whoever sits between developers and hundreds of competing models gains durable platform power as models commoditize. OpenRouter routes across 400+ models for roughly 8 million developers and processed ~1.5 quadrillion tokens in the past year; Stripe now controls the model-selection, metering, and billing layer of the emerging agent economy in one move. Thompson's neutrality framing is a direct echo of D&B's own 'be everywhere' positioning — the entity that sits between users and fragmented AI infrastructure, trusted by all sides, captures compounding value. For D&B, this validates the Visa analogy: the neutral data layer embedded into every agent workflow is the structural position worth owning, and the market just priced that thesis at $7–8 billion for a router alone.

stories.headline: Nvidia's Risky Business: Finding New Ways for Customers to Raise Money Expands AI Buildout Risk Significantly
stories.summary: Published August 11 on Stratechery, Thompson's analysis examines Nvidia's move to help customers finance AI infrastructure purchases — effectively extending credit risk into the hardware layer and amplifying the already-precarious capital structure of the AI buildout. The piece connects directly to the unresolved demand question: capex is front-loaded, but enterprise revenue justifying it has not yet materialized at scale, and Nvidia's financing maneuver raises the stakes if the adoption curve disappoints. For D&B, this is a signal that the AI infrastructure bet is increasingly leveraged, making the value of provable ROI — exactly what D&B's decision-intelligence layer can demonstrate through measurable pipeline and risk outcomes — more commercially urgent for enterprise buyers. It also flags a macro risk to watch: a financing crunch at the infrastructure layer could sharply accelerate enterprise pressure to show AI value, compressing D&B's window to land as the trusted data foundation before austerity resets priorities.

stories.headline: Trusted Agentic AI Landscape Q3 2026: Enterprise Vendor Selection, Sovereignty, and Lock-in
stories.summary: Published August 4, 2026, practitioner analyst Kai Waehner's Q3 landscape maps every major enterprise agentic AI vendor on two axes — trust and lock-in — arguing that the vendor decision in 2026 is fundamentally a governance and sovereignty decision, not a capability one. The piece concludes that 'clean, current, connected data is what separates an agent you can trust from one you cannot,' and that enterprises must design the data and integration layer first, with the AI vendor decision sitting on top of it. This is a near-perfect third-party validation of D&B's foundational positioning: entity resolution, verified business data, and explainable signals are not features of the AI layer — they are the precondition for trustworthy agentic action, making D&B's role infrastructure rather than application. The trust-vs-lock-in framing also reinforces D&B's neutrality advantage: an independent, platform-agnostic data layer scores high on trust and low on lock-in, the quadrant enterprises are explicitly hunting for.

data_science.topic: dbt (data build tool) — Transforming Raw Data into Trusted Analytics
data_science.tagline: SQL-first data transformation that brings software engineering discipline — version control, testing, documentation — to the analytics layer.
data_science.what_it_is: dbt (data build tool) is an open-source transformation framework that lets analytics engineers write modular SQL SELECT statements ('models') and have dbt handle the materialisation, dependency resolution, testing, and documentation automatically. It sits between your raw data warehouse (Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, Redshift) and your downstream consumers — BI tools, ML pipelines, AI agents. The core philosophy is 'EL + T': someone else loads raw data into the warehouse; dbt owns the Transform. Every model is a plain .sql file, every transformation is auditable and version-controlled in Git, and every output can be tested with assertions. The result is a governed, trustworthy analytics layer — exactly what AI agents and ML models need as their ground truth.
data_science.how_it_works: 1. MODELS: Each .sql file is a model — a SELECT query that dbt compiles into a CREATE TABLE or CREATE VIEW statement. Models reference each other via the ref() macro (e.g. FROM {{ ref('stg_company_firmographics') }}), which builds a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) of dependencies automatically. 2. DAG & LINEAGE: dbt resolves the DAG and executes models in the correct order. You visualise the full lineage — raw source → staging → intermediate → mart — in the dbt Docs UI. This makes data provenance auditable. 3. MATERIALISATION STRATEGIES: models can be views (cheap, always fresh), tables (full rebuild each run), incremental (append/upsert only new rows — critical for 600M+ record datasets), or ephemeral (CTEs, no storage). Incremental models are the workhorse for large-scale entity data. 4. TESTS: dbt ships built-in schema tests — not_null, unique, accepted_values, relationships — declared in YAML. Custom tests can encode business logic (e.g. 'Paydex score must be between 1 and 100'). Tests run after each build and block promotion if they fail. 5. SOURCES & FRESHNESS: Raw tables are declared as sources with freshness SLAs. dbt source freshness checks alert you if upstream data stops arriving — catching pipeline failures before downstream models silently propagate stale data. 6. MACROS & JINJA: dbt uses Jinja templating, allowing reusable SQL macros — parameterised logic you call like functions. A single 'clean_phone_number' macro applied consistently across all staging models prevents divergent cleaning logic. 7. DOCUMENTATION: Every model and column can have a description in YAML. dbt generates a searchable, interactive data catalogue automatically — the semantic layer for human and agent consumers to understand what each field means.
data_science.when_to_use: Use dbt when: (a) your raw warehouse data needs repeated, auditable transformation before ML or AI consumption — staging, joining, aggregating, deduplicating; (b) multiple teams or agents query the same underlying data and you need a single source of truth rather than bespoke per-notebook SQL; (c) data quality assertions must be enforced systematically, not just hoped for; (d) you are building a feature store layer on top of a data warehouse and want lineage traceability from raw event to ML feature; (e) you need incremental processing at scale — refreshing only new/changed records rather than rebuilding 600M rows every run. Avoid dbt for real-time streaming transformations (use Spark Structured Streaming or Flink instead) or compute-heavy Python transformations that cannot be expressed in SQL.
data_science.worked_example: D&B Context — Building the 'Account Intelligence Mart' for Agentforce and Copilot Agents. Raw inputs in Snowflake: (1) D&B entity master (DUNS, legal name, corporate family tree, SIC codes), (2) Paydex and Buydex scores (monthly snapshots), (3) CRM opportunity data (Salesforce export), (4) web intent signals (third-party feed). Step 1 — Staging models: stg_entity_master.sql cleans and casts raw entity fields; stg_paydex_history.sql deduplicates monthly score rows and enforces not_null and range tests (Paydex 1–100). Step 2 — Intermediate models: int_corporate_family.sql uses a recursive CTE to flatten parent–subsidiary trees to a single 'ultimate parent DUNS' per entity. int_buying_window.sql joins Buydex trend data with opportunity close dates to calculate 'months_to_likely_purchase' per account — the temporal analytics signal. Step 3 — Mart model: mart_account_intelligence.sql is the single wide table exposed to all agents. It joins entity firmographics, current Paydex, buying window score, open pipeline value, and subsidiary count. Materialised as an incremental table — only accounts with changed Paydex or new intent signals are reprocessed each day. dbt Tests enforce: DUNS uniqueness, Paydex not_null, relationship integrity back to entity master. The Prospecting Agent and Account Expansion Agent both query mart_account_intelligence via a vector DB or direct SQL tool call — and because every column has a dbt YAML description, the agent's LLM context knows exactly what 'buydex_percentile_rank' means without hallucinating. Result: a governed, tested, lineage-documented ground truth layer that makes every downstream AI agent more accurate and explainable — D&B's 'trusted data layer' strategy implemented in code.
resources: dbt Official Documentation — docs.getdbt.com: the canonical reference covering models, tests, sources, materialisations, macros, and the dbt Cloud vs dbt Core distinction
'The dbt Book' by Packt / Noah Kennedy: a practitioner-focused walkthrough of building production dbt projects on Snowflake and BigQuery, including CI/CD integration and advanced incremental patterns

dbt Learn Free Courses (learn.getdbt.com) — Fundamentals and Advanced tracks: hands-on, browser-based SQL labs that take you from your first model through to environment promotion and orchestration with Airflow or Dagster
